content: I just realised that I am getting automatic style fixes for that. That's quite cool. Since when is it enabled?

Ah I see, first time I saw the commit.

I just thought that general formatting could be done in CI, which would be a huge deal.

An official formatter hasn't been released yet, but yeah

Mathlib's pre-commit currently only removes trailing whitespace, makes sure the last line of the file ends with an EOL, and fixes some annoying line-ending issues for Windows users that haven't configured git/vscode right
This topic was moved here from #PR reviews > Is pre commit CI enabled? by Anne Baanen.
(I'll move this to mathlib4 since it is not directly about reviewing any particular PR.)
Ah, true. I put it in PR reviews since I noticed it during a PR.

Snir Broshi said:

An official formatter hasn't been released yet, but yeah

... but Marc Huisinga at the Lean FRO is working hard on this, so this will change. Getting this right takes time, but I look forward to that moment!

Michael Rothgang said:

Snir Broshi said:

An official formatter hasn't been released yet, but yeah

... but Marc Huisinga at the Lean FRO is working hard on this, so this will change. Getting this right takes time, but I look forward to that moment!

Would releasing a beta version now be helpful, benefiting from user feedback?

I should have probably announced this earlier, but #44573 refactors our pre-commit.ci setup to add the style lint fixes (mk_all, lint-style --fix and lint-bib.sh) which can be automatically fixed by lake exe lint-style --fix. So if this PR is merged, be aware that pre-commit.ci may become a bit more aggressive in pushing commits to PRs.

(By the way, one of my original motivations for this work was to ensure that PRs created by splice-bot would get the mk_all fixes automatically as well, but for various technical reasons related to GitHub's permissions that isn't possible with this approach. I'll try to get that working in a future PR.)
